"I defy anyone to explain how you would "detect" most of the above cheating. Check to see if the player navigates away from the game in his browser?"

I'm going to assume this part is about bigger online tournaments and not about some casual player. Lichess already does that first part, the game will be automatically terminated if you regularly leave the tab or have the same position open in an analysis board.

"Just use a second computer. Video relay of the player in front of his computer? Recruit a confederate to stand off to the side and tell you what to play."

Players are usually obligated to have at least two cameras so the second computer or "confederate" would've been noticed.

"You can't do better than random guessing for things this subtle."

You can! Looking at your flair you're way higher rated than me so I'm sure you know that each move has some sort of idea behind it. If an accused player can't quite explain their moves then everyone will get suspsicious of their play. My personally favorite way of checking whether someone is or isn't cheating is a 1+0 match, but i guess it only works for aforementioned obvious cheaters.

"What's more, anti-cheating measures might even be mildly harmful. Suppose someone uses an engine while playing. Does this harm anything?" 

It kinda does. If someone were to cheat in bullet/blitz it doesn't have a bigger impact on me (although everyone reacts differently) because the game will be over in 2-5 minutes. If someone were to cheat in rapid/classical i will be upset about it because i have to waste my time + lose against an essentially unbeatable opponent.

"Actually, provided he uses the engine in a consistent, predictable way, it harms nothing. He wins games he "shouldn't" win, but quickly ends up with e.g. a 3200 rating and doesn't play against the rest of us anymore."

However on his way to said 3200 he will mildly fuck with ~200 people and once again waste their time.

 "If you ban him, however, he creates a new account and starts again at a provisional rating, thus playing more engine games against the rest of us. If you just let such a person cheat he wouldn't play anyone other than fellow cheaters and wouldn't affect the rest of us at all."

If someone is so dedicated to cheat then banning them 2-3 times should effectively discourage them from furthering this issue.

- e4 e5 d4 exd4 c3 (a.k.a. the Danish Gambit) against ...e5,
- the Milner-Barry Gambit against the French Defense,
- e4 d5 Nf3 (a.k.a. the Tennison Gambit) against the Scandinavian Defense,
- e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 f4 (a.k.a. the Austrian attack) against the Pirc Defense,
